skill.name: audit
skill.description: Audit a codebase for quality gaps, TODOs, deprecated code, type issues, architecture problems, and code smells.

content.user_title: Audit Code Quality and Technical Debt
content.value_statement: Codebases can hide TODOs, deprecated APIs, type gaps, and architecture drift. This skill guides a systematic audit and produces a structured report.
actual_capabilities: Builds a file list for the requested audit scope.
Checks files for TODOs, deprecated code, type issues, and code smells.
Looks for architectural issues such as coupling, circular dependencies, and inconsistent patterns.
Uses TypeScript, linting, and grep-style checks when project tools are available.
Assigns severity levels to each finding.
Creates a structured markdown audit report with counts and top findings.
limitations: It identifies issues but does not fix code.
Automated checks depend on tools already configured in the repository.
Large repositories may require a narrowed scope.
Findings still need human review before prioritization.

use_cases.title: Pre-release Quality Review
use_cases.description: Run a structured review before a release to find type risks, stale work, and maintainability issues.

use_cases.title: Technical Debt Inventory
use_cases.description: Create a grouped list of debt, code smells, and architecture concerns for planning work.

use_cases.title: Repository Onboarding Audit
use_cases.description: Map common quality issues and conventions before contributing to an unfamiliar codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Audit This Repository
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of the current workspace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for TODOs, deprecated code, type issues, architecture problems, and code smells. Create a structured report.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Area
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a selected folder or package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the selected package only. Focus on maintainability, type safety, duplication, and architectural consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Before Release
prompt_templates.scenario: Release readiness review with automated checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the release branch. Run configured type and lint checks after confirming the commands with me.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Architecture Debt
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across modules and patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit cross-file architecture risks. Identify coupling, circular dependencies, inconsistent patterns, and systemic technical debt.

output_examples.input: Audit the frontend package before release.
output_examples.output: The report lists files reviewed, issue counts by severity, top findings, type check results, and lint findings.

output_examples.input: Find technical debt in the services folder.
output_examples.output: The audit groups findings by deprecations, TODOs, architecture issues, type issues, and code smells.

output_examples.input: Review this repository for onboarding risks.
output_examples.output: The summary highlights repeated patterns, naming inconsistencies, high-risk modules, and areas needing maintainer review.

best_practices: Confirm the audit scope before starting a large repository review.
Approve any local commands before the skill runs project tooling.
Review the final report with maintainers before creating tickets.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for security testing.
Do not run project scripts from an untrusted repository without approval.
Do not treat every reported smell as equally urgent.

faq.question: Does this skill change source files?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for read-only analysis and writes an audit report.

faq.question: Can it run automated checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest TypeScript, lint, and build checks when they are available.

faq.question: Should I approve commands first?
faq.answer: Yes. Approve local commands before running project scripts or build tools.

faq.question: What languages does it support?
faq.answer: It is most specific for TypeScript projects, but the review process can apply to many codebases.

faq.question: Does it prioritize fixes?
faq.answer: It reports severity and evidence. Planning fixes is a separate step.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
